article.title: California’s Tallest and Most Iconic Trees Are Getting Heatstroke
article.summary:
A grove of coast redwood trees is a forest of forests.
This means trees are slowing their “breathing” and “eating” because they can’t cool down fast enough when temperatures rise.
Trees use the pores in their leaves, stomata, to do two things: take carbon dioxide in, and let water out.
Open stomata mean the tree is “breathing” in carbon dioxide and photosynthesizing, but probably also letting water out.
Closed stomata mean the tree is conserving water but also slowing down its photosynthesis, since it isn’t taking in any carbon dioxide.

A major river in Nepal has flooded, sweeping away houses, bridges and damaging a part of hydropower station, authorities have said.
A video of the flood shows the moment raging waters sweep down a valley and wash away an entire building complex.
The flood swept away about a dozen houses and several suspension bridges, while a hydroelectric project was damaged, carrying some of the construction equipment away, the disaster management authority said.
"We are yet to see the full scale of the damage, but they may have lost their homes, schools and communities.
Nepal is prone to disasters, from earthquakes to landslides and floods, as a result of the unpredictable natural environment in the Himalayas.

article.title: Burnham says it is 'clear' Russia interfered with Brexit referendum
article.summary:
Andy Burnham has said Russia did interfere with the Brexit referendum and warned that similar activities were taking place in France and Germany.
Burnham did not provide further details about the type or extent of Moscow's activity during the Brexit referendum.
Doughty also denied that Burnham was raising the issue of Russian interference in the Brexit referendum because he wants to rejoin the EU.
In his interview, due to be released on Monday, Burnham said he had discussed the problem of Russian interference with Chancellor Friedrich Merz during his visit to Germany earlier this week.
"There is certainly misinformation, disinformation that is emanating from Russia into German politics," he said.

article.title: UK can’t rely on AI that could be switched off, Turing chief tells Guardian
article.summary:
The UK must not depend on foreign AI that could be cut off at short notice, the new head of the Alan Turing Institute has said.
“We shouldn’t depend solely on systems we can’t inspect or control, or that could be restricted or even switched off,” Williamson said.
He pointed to defence, national security, critical infrastructure and healthcare as areas where AI is now built in.
Williamson said the UK should have some AI it does not need anyone’s permission to use.
The institute cannot match the budgets of big AI labs, he added, but it could build smaller, nationally owned models for start-ups.

article.title: Eritrea urges UN to intervene in standoff with Ethiopia
article.summary:
Share Eritrea urges UN to intervene in standoff with Ethiopia on social mediaEritrea has asked the United Nations to take “deterrent measures” after what it called Ethiopia’s “declaration of war” in the conflict over the Tigray region.
The neighbouring countries have accused each other of starting a war over Tigray, where Ethiopia says Eritrea is backing rebels.
Ethiopian Foreign Minister Gedion Timothewos on Friday accused Eritrea of “a blatant act of aggression that engages Ethiopia’s inherent right to self-defence”.
Eritrean Information Minister Yemane Gebremeskel accused Ethiopia on Friday of pursuing aggression against Eritrea through its demands for sovereign access to the Red Sea.
Eritrea gained independence from Ethiopia in 1993, and they fought a deadly border war from 1998 to 2000.

article.title: High silver prices threaten Lucknow’s famed bridal nagra craft
article.summary:
The small workshop sits beside Chowk Bazaar, one of Old Lucknow’s oldest and busiest markets, a famed hub for wedding shopping full of silver jewellery and handcrafts.
For three decades, Hussain has been one of the bazaar’s busiest craftsmen, making a distinctive form of silver slip-on shoes, known locally as nagras.
Craftsmen have used this process to make silver nagras since the 1600s.
Once reserved exclusively for Nawabs, silver nagras have become a cherished wedding tradition over the last century, embraced by Lucknow’s middle and upper classes alike.

article.title: Putin tells Trump peace talks are unlikely, cites Ukraine drone attacks
article.summary:
Negotiators aim to present a proposal to Russia in the coming weeks, meanwhile Putin says resumption of talks unlikely.
Russian President Vladimir Putin has said an immediate resumption of peace talks with Ukraine is unlikely, citing drone attacks on Moscow during parliamentary elections last month.
In a phone call with US President Donald Trump on Friday, Putin said Moscow was ready to resume negotiations with Kyiv after the parliamentary elections.
However, the drone attacks on the capital made the resumption of trilateral peace talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US unlikely.
“As the president said, we will now assess when these negotiations can resume,” he added regarding the trilateral talks.

article.title: Is NZ’s foreign policy ‘realism’ working? Why the next government faces a real choice
article.summary:
With the core principles of an independent New Zealand foreign policy – support for a rules-based international order and multilateralism – under sustained attack, Foreign Minister Winston Peters recently reflected on his government’s response during the past three years.
He told the Institute of International Affairs the country had faced “the worst international conditions since 1945”.
Instead, it pursues a global order based on a US-led concert of great powers.
From this perspective, New Zealand’s current “softly softly” foreign policy, especially toward the US, can be seen as anything but realistic.
Or it can begin the task of realigning its foreign policy to deepen cooperation with other small and middle powers that, like New Zealand, depend on a functioning international rules-based order.

article.title: Countries warn against travel to Saudi Arabia following Houthi attacks
article.summary:
Share Countries warn against travel to Saudi Arabia following Houthi attacks on social mediaSeveral countries have warned their citizens against travel to Saudi Arabia following a series of Houthi attacks on airports in the kingdom.
Australia’s Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade said Australians should avoid King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and “reconsider” travel to other Saudi airports.
Global Affairs Canada issued an advisory against non-essential travel to any part of Saudi Arabia.
The warnings come as Saudi Arabia reels from five attacks on its airports in less than a week.
King Khalid international airport and King Fahd international airport in Dammam remain closed following the attacks, causing significant disruption to aviation across the Middle East.
